title: Choosing an optimization algorithm
summary: Pick grid for tiny discrete spaces, montecarlo for broader random sampling, and GA/SA/PSO/bayesian for harder or expensive searches. Sample-count knobs live on the config card.
narrative:
opti_method selects how the search walks Parameter space:

- grid — exhaust or coarse-grid small, mostly discrete spaces.
- montecarlo — random samples when the space is larger.
- GA — genetic search for mid-to-large mixed spaces.
- SA — simulated annealing when local optima are a risk.
- PSO — particle swarm, stronger on continuous spaces.
- bayesian — few expensive evaluations when each trial is costly.

Prefer grid or a small montecarlo when dimensions are few. Prefer bayesian or GA/PSO when you need fewer steps in a larger space. How many samples opti_sample_count buys, and how many Top-K rows to keep, belong on the optimize config card—not here. This card does not invent default hyperparameters or performance numbers.
